title: Raise the level by handing over thinking
statement: Raise a course's level by handing students more of the thinking, such as framing questions, choosing evidence, handling ambiguity and repairing their own reasoning, not by harder vocabulary alone.
detail: Review found the first conventional Grade 9 plan basic beside the Grade 3 work (`g9/transcript/chat-transcript.redacted.txt`, lines 2534 and 2555), and inspection confirmed that the Grade 3 lessons already teach children to weigh competing clues, justify the strongest evidence, combine quotation with knowledge, predict consequences and transfer a rule from one story to another (line 2620). The plan was rebuilt around increasingly independent intellectual work, and that resource was endorsed (lines 2622 and 2705). The later design brief defines advanced learning as greater responsibility for framing questions, choosing evidence and handling ambiguity, adds that more difficult vocabulary alone does not raise the level of thinking, and has students formulate questions, distinguish plausible explanations, test counterfactuals, respond to counterevidence and repair their own reasoning (lines 2884 and 3085).
against: It has not been tested with students.

evidence.quote: Advanced learning means greater responsibility for framing questions, choosing evidence and handling ambiguity. More difficult vocabulary alone does not raise the level of thinking.
